chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He gave a ruling concerning a man whose family thought he had died or been killed, so his wife married or his concubine was married, and each of the two gave birth to a child from her new husband. Then the first husband returned or the master of the concubine returned. He said, so the ruling in that matter is: 'The first husband takes his wife, for he is more entitled to her, and the master takes his concubine and her child, or he takes from the price the price of the child with his consent.'

key_terms.قَضَى: He ruled / gave a legal verdict

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a husband returns after his wife remarried due to his presumed death?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the legal status of 'presumed death' (ghaybah) where a husband or master is absent, allowing his wife or concubine to remarry or be given in marriage. Upon the return of the original husband or master, he holds the primary right to reclaim his wife and the children born during her absence, or alternatively, to accept compensation for the child's value. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach to resolving familial and property disputes arising from uncertainty in lineage and marital status.
